thread:
mira: @here I'm seeing a spike in 5xxs from west-eu2 edge-pop (w-eu2-edge-3). Alerting now via pager. traffic shows ~40% loss for egress routes to our CDN peers.
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2165432100 - west-eu2 edge-pop degraded - pager triggered (sev2)
sanjay: oncall taking, digging into why KV cache miss rate jumped. starting from LB and NAT gateways.
mira: thanks. quick customer impact summary: hosted API latency up ~250-800ms for affected prefixes, token throughput down ~30%. A few enterprise customers in EU might see request failures.
nicole: grabbing logs from the edge instances, ssh-ing to w-eu2-edge-3.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Last deploy to w-eu2-edge-3 at 2165428000 by james - rollout completed. No rollback events recorded.
james: pinged infra team on potential kernel update this morning. will check node health + recent kernel messages.
eve-support: pre-drafting customer notice - do we have an ETA?
sanjay: ETA unknown, isolating whether it's network peering or local NAT saturation. Traffic graphs show pps spike around 2165430000. Running `tcptraceroute` and `ss` on host now.
mira: operational priority: 1) reduce customer-impacting egress failures (reroute where possible), 2) restore edge-pop health, 3) postmortem.
sanjay: temporary mitigation: update smart routing policy to avoid w-eu2-edge-3 and shift to w-eu2-edge-1/edge-2 and eu-central1 pop. Implementing route divert now (will add bypass rule for 2165432150).
nicole: pushed iptables NAT conntrack tune on w-eu2-edge-3 to relieve saturation. still high conntrack usage but dropping.
james: infra confirms a peering flap to peer-A in that PoP. Peering team engaging.
mira: Statuspage draft (public):
> We are investigating increased errors and latency for API requests originating in the west-eu2 region. Affected customers may see failed requests or higher latency. Our team is actively mitigating by diverting traffic and working with peering partners. Next update in 15 minutes.
eve-support: Customer email template (short):
> Hi <Customer>,
> We detected increased errors and latency for traffic routed through west-eu2 since ~07:20 UTC. We have applied automated routing changes to reduce impact and are working with our network partner to fully restore service. We'll follow up with an update in 30 minutes or sooner.
> Apologies for the disruption.
> —The Redwood Inference Ops Team
mira: Internal ops comms (for SEs/AE):
> Short summary: West-eu2 edge-pop experiencing partial egress failures due to a peering flap. Traffic has been rerouted; some EU customers may see transient failures. No customer data exposure. Escalation: Network team + Peering vendor engaged. Contact: @sanjay (oncall) for technical Qs.
sanjay: routing change applied: `smart-route add-exclude w-eu2-edge-3 --until 2165436000` and `reroute -region eu-central1 –weight 60%` — verifying propagation.
nicole: I see the 5xx rate dropping from 42% -> 15% post-reroute. RTT still elevated for a subset of prefixes.
jeames: typo — meant james. Confirming peering vendor reports ongoing flap, ETA unknown.
mira: Handoff plan: current oncall (sanjay) will run primary until 2165433000; if unresolved, hand to nights (james). Please add status updates to the thread.
eve-support: Notifying top 10 affected customers with the template now; marking SEs for priority accounts.
sanjay: quick checklist we're doing in parallel:
- confirm NAT / conntrack levels (done, tuned)
- route divert completed (done)
- peering partner aware (in progress)
- edge instance health checks (restarting services scoped to PoP)
- status page + customer comms (mira/eve-support)
mira: Can we assemble a per-region status blurb for the ops command center? I'll post a short table: 
Region status summary:
- west-eu2: Partial egress failures, traffic rerouted to eu-central1 and other west-eu2 pops, 5xx rate decreasing, oncall engaged.
- eu-central1: Accepting diverted traffic, capacity headroom okay, monitoring for CPU / KV cache pressure.
- northamerica-west1: Unaffected.
- ap-south1: Unaffected.
sanjay: adding a quick internal runbook snippet in case we need to roll further: 
```
If PoP peering flap persists >30m:
 1) Shift 80% traffic to eu-central1 and 20% to west-eu1
 2) Increase caching TTLs for hot prefixes
 3) Disable non-essential background sync jobs in west-eu2
 4) Open support ticket with peering vendor, request BGP reset on affected session
```

mira: Good. Please record any customer escalations here.
eve-support: Two customers opened tickets: ACME (EU) and NimbusAnalytics — ACME seeing 502s intermittently. I've linked their ticket IDs.
sanjay: I've initiated a targeted canary to test end-to-end requests through eu-central1 — 20/20 successes. Load shaping looks healthy.
nicole: monitoring: 5xx now down to 7% and trending. conntrack stable after tune.
mira: Next public status page update: "Mitigations applied; traffic rerouted. Errors decreasing. Investigating root cause with peering partner. Next update in 30 minutes."
jeames: (infra) peering vendor expects BGP convergence within the hour after their adjustments.
sanjay: no new on-call alarms. I'll remain primary until 2165433000 and then handoff to james if still open.
mira: thx all — keep this thread as the single source for status page text and customer templates. After resolved, we'll run a focused postmortem on peering resilience and routing fallbacks.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2165432100 - mitigations applied; severity reduced to sev3 at 2165432187
sanjay: closing note: service largely stabilized, will monitor for 60m then clear incident if no regression.
mira: Noted. If anything changes ping @here. :thumbsup:
